title: Policy-driven export scheduler and tenant delivery dashboard for compliance evidence
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood customers (especially enterprise tenants) require automated, auditable evidence exports (PDF/CSV) for periodic compliance reporting, legal discovery, and internal attestations. Current exports are ad-hoc and lack: per-tenant residency routing, retention-aware inclusion/exclusion, delivery status visibility for tenants, and robust retry/fallback semantics.

Problem statement:
- Exports must respect tenant-level data residency and residency-aware storage sinks (regional S3/GCS buckets or on-prem bundles).
- Export contents must enforce retention/erasure rules so that records past retention policies are excluded or redacted according to policy.
- Operators and customers need a tenant-facing, real-time delivery dashboard that shows scheduled runs, last successful export, signed manifests, and failure reasons.
- Exports must be schedulable with timezone & business-day awareness and support PDF/CSV formats, encryption-at-rest, signed manifests, and verifiable checksums.

Proposal summary:
Build a policy-driven Export Orchestrator and Tenant Delivery Dashboard that:
1) Takes tenant export policies (residency, retention windows, allowed export formats),
2) Runs scheduled jobs per tenant with timezone/business-day semantics,
3) Produces format variants (PDF summary + CSV raw),
4) Stores artifacts in residency-appropriate sinks with KMS/HSM-wrapped keys,
5) Emits a signed manifest (SHA256 + signature) and stores lineage metadata in the compliance ledger,
6) Surfaces delivery status to tenants and ops via a new dashboard and webhook notifications, and
7) Supports manual ad-hoc exports and an approval gating flow for regulated tenants.

Key constraints and non-goals:
- This work focuses on export orchestration, residency routing, retention enforcement, and dashboarding. It does NOT include a full legal-discovery viewer or deep content redaction heuristics (those belong to a follow-up).
- We will rely on existing runtime export workers (ENG-61022) and the storage vault adapters (ENG-60511) with small adapter changes for residency flags.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Tenant can configure an export policy that specifies: format (PDF/CSV), destination sink (regional S3/GCS or on-prem transfer), retention window enforcement, cadence (cron or business-day), and timezone.
AC2: Scheduler executes on configured cadence; exported artifacts are placed in the residency-appropriate sink and include a signed manifest (SHA256 + KMS signature) and a JSON metadata ledger entry.
AC3: Retention rules are applied at export generation time: data older than tenant-specified retention is excluded or redacted and the manifest indicates redaction reasoning.

AC4: Tenant Delivery Dashboard shows per-tenant: next scheduled run, last run timestamp, artifact links, status (Success|Partial|Failed), and failure reason. Dashboard updates within 30s of job completion/failure.
AC5: Delivery supports retries with exponential backoff and falls back to alternate sink when primary sink returns 5xx; failures generate an alert to SRE and a webhook to tenant if configured.
AC6: All export artifacts are encrypted with tenant-scoped KMS keys and audit logs are emitted to the central audit pipeline with export identifiers.
AC7: Manual ad-hoc export UI is available with preview of estimated artifact size and retention-aware preview of row counts; manual exports are tracked in audit logs and respect residency routing.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement scheduler and manifest generation for a subset of internal tenants; expose dashboard behind feature flag. Target: 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (pilot): Enable for 5 external tenants (mix of hosted and Dedicated). Collect feedback on residency routing and retention edge-cases. Target: 3 weeks.
Phase 3 (GA): Enable self-serve policy UI in Console, expand to all tenants, and publish runbooks and compliance playbook. Target: console-2026.04 release.
Rollback: Disable scheduler via feature-flag; orphaned artifacts cleaned by background garbage collector respecting retention policy.
metrics: % of tenant exports completed successfully within SLA (target >= 99% for P0 tenants)
Mean time to detect and notify tenant of failed export (target < 5m)
Average export generation latency per GB (target < 3m/GB in hosted),
Reduction in manual export requests to Support by 60% over 3 months
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misapplication of retention rules could leak data. Mitigation: retention engine unit + integration tests, separate redaction audit logs, and SRE kill-switch on exports.
Risk: Regional sink misconfiguration causing cross-region egress. Mitigation: strict residency validation in orchestration, pre-flight dry runs that verify sink region, and alerts on mismatches.
Risk: Large exports saturating runtime. Mitigation: bandwidth throttling, chunked export generation, and off-peak scheduling for heavy tenants.
Risk: Tenant confusion about delivered contents. Mitigation: signed manifests with human-readable summary PDFs, and tenant-facing explanations in dashboard.
Risk: Key management complexity. Mitigation: reuse KMS integrations and ensure keys are tenant-scoped; include key-rotation tests.
